Summary of triage so far (quick notes):
- Initial signal: p95 jump correlates with increased small-sequence token fanout on gen-api checkout route. KV cache miss-rate up ~3x in the past 30m.
- No recent model rollouts or kernel changes in the last 24h from product side. Two customer traffic patterns shifted (longer prompt auth metadata).

Proposed immediate action (safe-first sequence):
1) SRE to enable conservative routing to fallback smaller-worker instances for the checkout route (5–10% traffic) to absorb any hot-path regressions. This is low-risk and reversible.
2) Defer non-critical background jobs (batch embeddings / index refresh) for 2 hours to free IO resources. Product can flip a flag.
3) NO quantization changes or aggressive compiler flags in the hotfix — those introduce risk to correctness and should be avoided during a live mitigation.
4) Prepare a low-verbosity customer message that explains we're investigating, impact limited to p95, and commit to a follow-up within 2 hours.

Longer-term asks (post-stabilize):
- Engineering to add a KV cold-start warmup during scaling events and an auto-prefetch for recent keys used by checkout flows.
- Product to evaluate a targeted canary for runtime memory tuning outside peak.

I can lead the customer note draft once SRE confirms steps 1–2 and a canary window.

Marissa
Director, Product Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment suggested: prod-deploy-checklist.pdf (we should follow before any patch)

Thanks — quick operational update and constraints:
- Confirmed KV miss-rate spike on the telemetry. Root cause not yet pinned; early hypothesis points to cache churn from a traffic fanout pattern (short-lived keys).
- We can spin a routing fallback quickly: configure 5% of checkout traffic to go to conservative-worker pool (smaller batch sizes, more aggressive prefix caching). Estimated time to change: 12 minutes.
- We'll schedule a controlled canary patch for 02:30–03:30 PT tonight (off-peak) to test a runtime parameter that reduces KV eviction aggressiveness by 15%. Canary will be 5% traffic, roll-forward if p95 improves and no error-rate uptick.
- Risk: the runtime param increases memory pressure ~8–12% on canary nodes. We'll monitor OOM/OOM-kill signals closely and have immediate rollback.

Requested from Product: confirm you want the routing fallback now + deferred background-job toggle. Product to provide flag names and owners.
Requested from CS (Kimberly): a two-sentence note to Cartful that doesn't overpromise. I'll include the checklist attachment before any deploy.

I'll attach the prod-deploy-checklist.pdf to the runbook and push the routing change once Alex approves customer comm.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Prod latency spikes impacting checkout — planned mitigations and canary window

Hi Jason / Cartful ops —

Thanks for the quick signal and attachments. Short update and plan:

What we observed: p95 latency elevated on the checkout route between ~08:45–09:10 PT; no error-rate increase noticed.
What we'll do now (timeline):
- Immediate: route 5% of Cartful checkout traffic to a conservative worker pool (started at 16:30 PT). Expected effect: reduce tail latency for most impacted sessions with no customer-visible config changes.
- Tonight, 02:30–03:30 PT: we'll run a controlled canary (5% traffic) to test a runtime memory parameter that reduces KV eviction aggressiveness. If canary shows p95 improvement and no increase in error-rate, we'll expand rollout. If we detect OOM or error-rate regressions we'll roll back within minutes.

Risk & mitigations: the canary increases memory on canary nodes by ~8–12%; SRE will monitor OOM and CPU closely and has an immediate rollback plan. No model or quantization changes will be made during this window.

Customer-facing note (short):
"We observed elevated tail latency on the checkout path affecting some customers this morning. We have implemented a conservative routing fallback and will run a controlled canary tonight (02:30–03:30 PT) to validate a stabilization parameter. We expect minimal disruption; we'll follow up with results by 04:00 PT tomorrow morning."

If that wording looks good, Kimberly will send the official note from Redwood to your ops alias. Please let me know if you need a different cadence or want us to open a joint status bridge.

Appreciate the heads-up and the log samples — they helped speed triage.

— Alex Martinez
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
